newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat futures end volatile day lower.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat futures end volatile day lower.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures closed sharply lower on improved planting prospects in North Dakota, forecasts for drought breaking rains in Europe, and estimates that the recent winterkill in the U.S. Great Plains may not have been as bad as previously thought, traders said.
Wheat futures were volatile with a late recovery short-lived, they said.
"We rallied when they saw the EU was taxing exports and then broke hard at the end. Then we saw a couple of stories that the winterkill wasn't as bad as thought," a trader said.
The EU Thursday slapped a tax of 15 Ecus per tonne on daily exports of soft wheat. Last week, the EU stopped its weekly wheat export tenders.
MGE spring wheat futures volume was estimated at 33.066 million bushels, above the 24.127 million bushels traded Wednesday.
MGE spring wheat futures closed 12-1/2 to 16-3/4 cents per bushel lower, with May down 16-3/4 at $4.37-1/2. July was down 14 at $4.40-1/2.
